title: Short Stuff: Exploring Irish Monk
summary: Short Stuff episode examining whether Irish monks reached North America before the Vikings. Josh and Chuck discuss the Viking settlement at L'Anse aux Meadows in Newfoundland, the legend of St. Brendan's sixth-century voyage in search of the Land of Promise of the Saints, the Navigatio sancti Brendani (Travels of St. Brendan) account, Norse saga clues about Irish presence in Greenland and North America, the disputed Horse Creek petroglyphs in West Virginia linked to ogham script (Barry Fell), the comparison of the Navigatio's fantastical elements to immram tales, and Tim Severin's curragh voyage showing the route was feasible. They conclude it is mostly folklore with possible kernels of truth.
topics: Land of Promise of the Saints

segments.title: Opening and Columbus myth
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck open the short stuff, joking that they aim to dispel the idea that Columbus discovered America and noting the Vikings were the first Europeans to reach North America.

segments.title: L'Anse aux Meadows and the St. Brendan legend
segments.summary: They describe the Viking settlement at L'Anse aux Meadows in Newfoundland, then introduce the legend of St. Brendan, a sixth-century Irish monk who supposedly sailed in search of the Land of Promise of the Saints and reached a vast land with fruit and gems.
topics: Land of Promise of the Saints

segments.title: Skepticism about Brendan's destination and the Navigatio
segments.summary: Chuck and Josh question where Brendan actually went, noting he was a skilled navigator. They mention the ninth-century Navigatio sancti Brendani, a widely translated account of the journey.

segments.title: Norse saga clues
segments.summary: The hosts describe Norse sagas that mention Irish missions already in Greenland and Newfoundland, encounters with Native Americans who had seen white men, and a tribe whose language sounded like Irish.

segments.title: Horse Creek petroglyphs
segments.summary: Barry Fell, a marine biologist, claimed petroglyphs in West Virginia were ogam script left by Irish visitors. Academics were skeptical, and the local archaeological society argued the carvings more likely came from local indigenous people.

segments.title: Folklore in the Navigatio and immram tales
segments.summary: Chuck and Josh describe the fantastical elements of the Navigatio, such as a griffin fight and an island that turned out to be a whale, and compare them to seventh and eighth century Irish immram voyage tales. They liken it to dressing up history in folklore.

segments.title: Tim Severin's curragh experiment
segments.summary: They discuss the curragh boat used by Brendan and how adventurer Tim Severin built one and retraced the route from Ireland to Iceland, Greenland and Newfoundland, showing the voyage was possible.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck conclude with a shrug and mention a HowStuffWorks article Josh wrote, then sign off.
